Sex-specific effects of the DAF-12 steroid receptor on aging in Caenorhabditis elegans. Sex differences in longevity and aging are seen throughout the animal kingdom. These are likely to result, in part, from sex differences in endocrinology. In the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans, males are the longer-lived sex. Here we explore the possibility that sex differences in insulin/insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) and steroid endocrinology contribute to this sex difference in aging by studying C. elegans populations in liquid culture.
